title: How to Clean a Glass Cooktop

seo.title: How to Clean a Glass Cooktop
seo.meta_description: Clean a cool glass cooktop with a compatible cleaner and soft pad; handle melted sugar according to the manual and avoid scratch-causing abrasives.
seo.search_intent: Clean a glass or ceramic cooktop without scratching it, damaging the finish, or turning burned spills into surface damage.

excerpt: A glass cooktop looks tough, but the surface can scratch. Remove grit first, use approved tools, and deal with spills before they become repeatedly burned-on layers.
content_html:
Let the cooktop cool unless the manual gives a specific procedure for melted sugar. Clean in layers: loose particles, grease, then stubborn residue.

Remove grit before rubbing

Wipe away salt, crumbs, and hard particles with a soft cloth. Dragging them under a pad can create fine scratches.

Use a cooktop cleaner or the product the manufacturer recommends

Apply a small amount, work it with a nonabrasive pad, and buff away residue. Too much product can leave a cloudy film.

Burned deposits may need an approved scraper

Use a cooktop razor scraper only if the appliance maker permits it, holding it at the recommended angle. Never use a damaged blade or improvise with a tool that can dig a corner into the glass.

Melted sugar and plastic are special cases

Some manufacturers instruct users to remove them while the surface is still warm because they can damage glass as they cool. Follow the model manual and protect your hands; do not guess at the procedure.

Avoid oven cleaner and harsh abrasives

Also avoid impacts from heavy cookware. If the surface is cracked, stop using the cooktop and follow the manufacturer’s power-isolation and service instructions.

A quick wipe after routine cooking keeps small splatters from becoming repeated burned-on deposits.

faq.question: Can I use a razor blade?
faq.answer: Only an approved cooktop scraper and only when the manufacturer permits that method.

faq.question: What should I do with melted sugar?
faq.answer: Check the manual promptly; some makers call for removal before the spill cools completely.

faq.question: Can I use oven cleaner?
faq.answer: Not unless the cooktop manufacturer specifically approves it; it may damage the surface.
